reason: The goal bear-trap-capture's first slice has landed: trapeffect_bear_trap()'s monster arm (C 1525-1558) is ported and js/trap_effects.js:491's refusal is gone. Six entries remain missing: the BEAR_TRAP-reachable subset of mintrap()'s mtrapped arm with trapname(), m_move()'s mtrapped prologue, and heal_legs() with the nh_timeout() case that reaches it. This checklist replaces the one that covered sit-command, finish-seed1150 and finish-seed0200, whose slices closed and whose evidence is recorded in GOALS.json, SCORE.tsv and QUALITY.json.

boundary.startingEvent: A monster completes a move onto a square holding a bear trap, so monmove.c postmov() calls mintrap() and its already-ported dispatch reaches trapeffect_selector(); or, for the third slice, any turn on which the hero's wounded-legs timeout counts down to zero in timeout.c nh_timeout(), which js/allmain.js:684 reaches every turn.
boundary.endingEvent: The trapped monster pulls free at mintrap()'s !rn2(40), and the hero's own bear-trap wound ends with heal_legs() drawing 'Your leg feels better.  Your movements are now unencumbered.' In seed0004-feeding-pony the boundary runs from step 34 to step 170; step 171 types a count prefix, which js/cmd.js:1920 refuses through readSimpleCommand(), and that refusal is the cap rather than part of this goal.
boundary.validInputs: Any seed, date and options whose D:1 places a bear trap a monster can walk onto, plus the hero walking onto one. seed0004-feeding-pony is the only development session that reaches the boundary: seed 4, datetime 20260414173108, OPTIONS=symset:DECgraphics, one segment. autopickup is off by its optlist.h:184 default, so js/hack.js:918 cannot interfere.
boundary.observables: Every screen, cursor and random-number call from the monster's completed move through the escape, and from the wounded-legs countdown through heal_legs(). The order-sensitive ones are d(2,4) at trap.c:1554, which C spends eleven keystrokes after the pline_mon() at 1534 suspends on a --More--, and the per-turn rn2(40) at trap.c:3751.
boundary.exclusions: The count prefix at step 171 and everything after it, including hack.c moverock() at step 203 and #loot at 238. dog.c keepdogs()'s trapped-follower line, refused at js/dog.js:657, which needs a level change while a pet is trapped. heal_legs()'s how == 1 dismount and how == 2 petrification arms. trapeffect_bear_trap()'s two remaining hero branches, the mounted arm at C 1507-1511 and the iron-shoes line at C 1517-1518, which preflight_dotrap() refuses ahead of the move. mintrap()'s pit and metallivore machinery, which no bear trap reaches.

The monster arm's helpers are all ported: wearing_iron_shoes() at js/trap_effects.js:150, thitm() at :348, seetrap() at :209, a_your[]/A_Your[] at :129-130, m_in_air() at js/monmove.js:653, Monnam() as capitalizedMonsterName() at js/do_name.js:238, set_msg_xy() as messageAt() at js/startup_a11y.js:294. heal_legs()'s are too: body_part() at js/polyself.js:187, vtense() at js/objnam.js:529, makeplural() at js/fruit.js:293, encumber_msg() at js/pickup.js:80. Short-circuits were traced rather than assumed: for BEAR_TRAP, is_pit() is false throughout, so C's `!rn2(40) || (is_pit(...) && m_easy_escape_pit(...))` never evaluates its second disjunct.
candidateListMethod.javascriptCrossCheck: grep for each C function name across js/ to separate a missing port from a partial one under the same name; grep for 'unsupported(' and the boundary error classes in js/trap_effects.js, js/unported_monster_actions.js and js/timeout.js to enumerate the refusal sites; grep for resolveTrappedMonster to find the injection at js/unported_monster_actions.js:712 and its seam at js/monmove.js:2503; grep for trapname across js/ returned no definition and five refusing callers.
candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: The escape message is the weakest evidence. seed0004's escape at step 83 is silent because canseemon() is false by then, and no screen in its 409 steps contains 'pulls free', so trapname()'s only consumer in this goal fires in no development session and needs a fresh case that keeps a trapped monster visible across a 1-in-40 roll. Getting a bear trap into a fresh case at all is unsolved for every slice: apply.c set_trap() is unported at js/apply.js:93, doapply() refuses the tool by object type at js/apply.js:275, and wizgenesis and wizmap are unported, so a seed search is the only route and its domain must be recorded first. A monster cannot be commanded onto a trap: a pet that has seen it avoids it through mon_knows_traps(), and displacing a pet swaps it onto the hero's square.

sourceReview: Every branch and helper reachable inside the boundary was traced against nethack-c/upstream/ rather than inferred, by the slice-selector at a4e9d83 and recorded here at 8a25741. The trace covered state, message order and random-number order: d(2,4) at trap.c:1554 sits eleven keystrokes after the pline_mon() at 1534 suspends, and rn2(40) at trap.c:3751 recurs once per trapped turn. Stubs, stops and partial implementations are identified individually above: four refusal sites (js/trap_effects.js:491 and :811, js/unported_monster_actions.js:229-230, js/timeout.js:277-280), one injection standing in for a real function (resolveTrappedMonster at js/unported_monster_actions.js:712, seam js/monmove.js:2503), one function absent from js/ entirely (trapname()), and one partial port that counts down but does not act (js/timeout.js's WOUNDED_LEGS handling). Two claims in the goal's own detail were corrected by this reading and are corrected here: the detail says lifting the trap arm without the unported_monster_actions.js gate 'earns nothing', but C's log shows that gate firing at the pony's next action at step 46, so slice 1 earns steps 34-45; and the detail's four refusal sites omit that trapname() has five refusing callers of which this goal lifts none, because each of the other four needs its own surrounding branch. Slice 1 landed the monster arm at 1525-1558 entire; the four refusal sites it names are now three, js/trap_effects.js:491 having been replaced by the arm itself. Two of the arm's six branches are recorded as cannot-occur rather than done because this boundary cannot reach them, and each carries the specific upstream condition that prevents it.
